name: Scotch Marmalade
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Cut fruit into thin slices and take out seeds
Put in an earthenware pan and cover with eight and one-half quarts of cold water
Let it stand for twenty-four hours
Boil quickly for two hours, then add sugar and boil again one and one-half hours
The seeds should be soaked for twenty-four hours in one pint of cold water; when ready to put in the sugar pour the liquid off them through a strainer and add to the oranges

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut fruit into thin slices and take out seeds
2. Put in an earthenware pan and cover with eight and one-half quarts of cold water
3. Let it stand for twenty-four hours
4. Boil quickly for two hours, then add sugar and boil again one and one-half hours
5. The seeds should be soaked for twenty-four hours in one pint of cold water; when ready to put in the sugar pour the liquid off them through a strainer and add to the oranges
